title: Denormalization truncation to zero allows free yield extraction with low-decimal reward tokens
description: The normalize-discount-denormalize pipeline truncates at 4 points, all favoring the claimer. For small yield amounts with low-decimal reward tokens (USDC, 6 decimals), the denormalization at line 704 divides by 10^12, and if the pre-division value is < 10^12, actualPayment becomes 0. The claimer receives real yield tokens (withdrawn at line 594) while paying nothing. There is no `if (actualPayment == 0) revert` check. Prior L-01 from stable-yield-accumulator-01 identified dust-level truncation, but this is a qualitative escalation: zero payment for non-zero yield is a concrete code defect enabling free value extraction.
impact: Claimer extracts yield tokens for free when actualPayment truncates to zero. Each free claim extracts less than 1 unit of the smallest denomination, but the attack is essentially costless (especially on L2s). The systematic rounding bias compounds over thousands of claims.
attack_path: Claimer calls claim() when pending yield is small enough (< 1e-6 USDC equivalent)
Strategy withdraws yield to claimer at line 594
recommendation: Add minimum payment check: `if (actualPayment == 0 && totalNormalizedYield > 0) revert ZeroAmount()`. Use ceiling division in _denormalizeAmount: `scaled = (scaled + divisor - 1) / divisor`.
